title: Non-Mendelian Inheritance Patterns
objectives: Identify five major non-Mendelian inheritance mechanisms
Explain genomic imprinting and uniparental disomy
Apply knowledge to genetic counseling scenarios

genomic_imprinting.title: Imprinting Disorders
genomic_imprinting.content:
Prader-Willi Syndrome
• Mechanism: Paternal 15q11-q13 deletion/maternal UPD
• Features: Hypotonia, hyperphagia, obesity
• Testing: DNA methylation analysis
Angelman Syndrome
• Mechanism: Maternal 15q11-q13 deletion/paternal UPD
• Features: Developmental delay, ataxia, happy demeanor
• Gene: UBE3A

mitochondrial.title: Mitochondrial Inheritance
mitochondrial.content:
• Maternal transmission only (sperm mitochondria degenerate)
  • Heteroplasmy: Mixed normal/mutant mtDNA (threshold effect)
  • Examples: MELAS (m.3243A>G), LHON (m.11778G>A)

uniparental_disomy.title: UPD Mechanisms
uniparental_disomy.content:
UPD Types and Consequences

Isodisomy: Identical chromosomes → recessive disorders (e.g., CF from carrier parent)

Heterodisomy: Both homologs from one parent → imprinting disorders

Testing: SNP microarray analysis

triplet_repeats.title: Dynamic Mutations
triplet_repeats.content:
Fragile X Syndrome

Gene: FMR1 (Xq27.3)
Normal: 5-44 CGG repeats
Premutation: 55-200 (risk of FXPOI/FXTAS)
Full mutation: >200 (methylation → silencing)

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
Why can imprinting disorders occur without DNA sequence changes?

Epigenetic silencing marks (DNA methylation/histone modifications) can be aberrantly reset during gametogenesis without altering the nucleotide sequence.

How does heteroplasmy explain variable mitochondrial disease severity?

Tissues with higher mutant mtDNA load (>60-80%) exceed the threshold for oxidative phosphorylation failure - explains why siblings may have different organ involvement.

Why does UPD of chromosome 7 cause Russell-Silver syndrome?

Maternal UPD7 leads to loss of paternally expressed growth-promoting genes (e.g., GRB10 at 7p12.2).
